title: Generate Equivalent Expressions
objective: I can use the commutative, associative, and identity properties to rewrite expressions.
model: rearranging and regrouping terms or factors without changing the value (4 × 17 × 25 = 4 × 25 × 17 = 100 × 17), and writing the identity element (a + 0, a × 1)

widgets.component: Prep Station: 3n + 4 at n = 5, like terms, 2n + 3n at n = 4, definition of equivalent
widgets.root: Review of 6-5/6-6 needed to talk about equivalence; keys 19, 4n and 7n, 20, 'same value for every value' recomputed.

widgets.component: First Course: name the property in 5 + 13 = 13 + 5, (6 × 3) × 2 = 6 × (3 × 2), 47 + 0 = 47, 8 × 5 to 5 × 8; '4 + 0 = 4 is commutative' error
widgets.root: Directly the objective; keys right and the err card (swapped places so it must be commutative) targets the identity/commutative mix-up. Distributive appears only as a distractor name.

widgets.component: Main Course: match six equations to property + operation; '(2 + 3) + 4 = (3 + 2) + 4 is associative'
widgets.root: Six pairs recomputed (commutative add/mult, associative add/mult, identity add/mult); the err card (parentheses present so grouping changed) is the right misconception.

widgets.where: Practice §3 item 3.2, §5 item 5.3; Challenge §5 item 5.2 (tbl, mc, num)
widgets.root: The lesson's idea is to reorder and regroup to make friendly numbers, which is a drag-and-regroup move, but in the studio the rearrangement is already printed (3.2 shows '25 × 4 × 7 = 100 × 7' and asks only for 700) or is one multiple-choice stem (5.3 4 × 17 × 25 = 1,700; C 5.2 asks for the product). Nothing lets the student perform or justify the rearrangement.
widgets.replacement: New act:regroup (assets/studio-act/regroup.js): a row of movable term/factor chips for an expression such as 4 × 17 × 25; dragging chips swaps order (log 'commutative') and tapping two adjacent chips draws a bracket (log 'associative'); a running line shows the current form and a bracket total (4 × 25 = 100); the task ends when the student has produced a form containing a power of ten product and typed the value (1,700). Graded by (a) every form equals the original value and (b) a friendly product was formed; wrong moves trapped: swapping across subtraction/division ('15 − 8' chips refuse to swap and say why) and changing numbers. Use it at L1 (+ chips), L2 (× chips), L3 (mixed with a variable). Replace P 3.2 and 5.3 and C 5.2 with it.

widgets.where: Practice §4 items 4.1-4.7 (gen:combineLikeTerms L1-L3, equivalentExpr L2-L3, act:tiles combine L2)
widgets.component: Remix Lab: like term of 4h, combine 5r + 2 − 3r, 'always true' equations, 'which is NOT equivalent', algebra tiles combining like terms
widgets.root: The lesson objective is to use the commutative, associative and identity properties to rewrite expressions; none of the seven items asks for a commutative, associative or identity move; they repeat 6-6 content (combining like terms), and equivalentExpr L2-L3 draws are 58% and 83% distributive. The distributive property (expand and factor) is derived in 6-14, and combining like terms after distributing in 6-15.
widgets.replacement: Re-author section 4 as a property remix: new gen 'propertyRewrite' L1 (name the property: commutative/associative/identity × add/mult, ties to 'which property lets you rearrange 8 × 5'), L2 ('which expression is equivalent by the associative property to (n + 2) + 6? key n + (2 + 6)'; 'what number makes n × □ = n? 1'), L3 (mental math with a variable: 'rewrite 4 × (n × 25) so a friendly product appears' key (4 × 25) × n = 100n). Use act:regroup (above) for 4.7.

widgets.component: Which property changes the ORDER / the GROUPING of factors; (8 + 5) + 2 = 8 + (5 + 2)
widgets.root: The objective; Commutative, Associative, Distributive, Identity choices with the usual order/grouping swap as distractors.
Collecting terms after reordering is the application of the commutative/associative properties named in the objective; 3n + 6 and 42 recomputed.

widgets.where: Challenge §1 items 1.1-1.5 (gen:combineLikeTerms L2-L4, equivalentExpr L2, L3)
widgets.component: Hot Line: combine like terms, 'always true', 'NOT equivalent', and simplify 4a + 3(a + 4) + 10
widgets.root: The lesson objective is to use the commutative, associative and identity properties to rewrite expressions; the section drills like terms and distributive forms; every L4 combine draw (300 of 300) distributes first and 58-83% of equivalentExpr L2-L3 draws need distributing. The distributive property (expand and factor) is derived in 6-14, and combining like terms after distributing in 6-15.
widgets.replacement: Replace the six-item climb with the propertyRewrite generator at L2-L4: L4 'Which property justifies each step in 12 + (n + 8) = 12 + (8 + n) = (12 + 8) + n = 20 + n? (commutative, then associative)' and 'which step is NOT allowed (reordering a subtraction)'.

widgets.component: 'Leo says 4m + 7 and m + 25 are not equivalent. Which reasoning proves Leo is right?'
widgets.root: Two choices are defensible: 'Try m = 4: 23 and 29. One test is not enough to decide' is false (one value with different results is enough to prove non-equivalence), and the key needs a decoy first test that matches. The item teaches that a counterexample needs company.
widgets.replacement: Same rewrite as 6-6: stem 'Which test PROVES not equivalent?' key 'Try m = 4: 23 and 29. The values differ, so they are not equivalent.'; distractors 'Try m = 6: both 31, so they are equivalent', 'They look different', 'Try m = 4 and m = 4 again'.

widgets.where: Challenge §2 items 2.1, 2.4-2.7 (err, mc, num, mc, mc)
widgets.component: Order Tickets: subtraction is not commutative error, Cook A vs Cook B tray weights, catering quote 9 + 4n + 11 + 2n, flour 5 − 12, n + n + n + n + 6
widgets.root: Recomputed: equivalent via reordering then 14 + 6 = 20; 6n + 20 = 50 at n = 5; 5 − 12 = −7 vs 12 − 5 = 7; 4n + 6. These are the lesson's contrast between operations that commute and those that do not.

widgets.component: Expression → Rearranged → Property Used → Value for 2 × 13 × 50 and 45 + 27 + 55
widgets.root: Four of six cells are free text graded by exact string: '2 × 50 × 13 = 100 × 13', '45 + 55 + 27 = 100 + 27' and 'Commutative & Associative' twice; a student cannot type × or & on the decimal keypad (inputmode=decimal), and 'commutative and associative', '100 × 13 = 1300' or any other correct reorder is marked wrong.
widgets.replacement: Use act:regroup (above) for the rearrangement, a two-option select for 'Property used' (Commutative / Associative / Both) and keep the numeric Value cells (1300, 127). Also normalise whitespace, × / x and & / and in K.tbl for any remaining text cell.

widgets.component: Algebra tiles: combine like terms such as 3x + 5 − 4x + 1
widgets.root: The lesson objective is to use the commutative, associative and identity properties to rewrite expressions; the activity is collecting like tiles, 6-6 and 6-15 content, not rewriting with a property.

Equivalent mode is distribution of a multiplier over a binomial with negative tiles. The distributive property (expand and factor) is derived in 6-14, and combining like terms after distributing in 6-15.
widgets.replacement: Replace with act:regroup L3 (see Practice §3) and move the tile task to 6-14.

widgets.component: Sort six pairs as equivalent for every n or not (8 + n / n + 8, n − 3 / 3 − n, n ÷ 5 / 5 ÷ n …)
widgets.root: Exactly the commutative-versus-non-commutative contrast; bins recomputed.

widgets.component: Food Critic: 24 ÷ n commutes, parentheses mean associative, n + n + n = n³, 7 × 0 is the identity
widgets.root: Each error sits at the named step (Step 1, Step 2, Step 2) and 4.4 key (only multiplication by 1) is right.

widgets.component: Head Chef Boss: associative multiplication, 7 + 3n + 8 + n, FALSE statement, 1 × n + 0 + n × 1
Why commutative works for + and × but not − and ÷; create your own expression with three terms
widgets.root: Pass on 40 characters and self-ticked rubric lines.
widgets.replacement: Require two numeric boxes (15 − 8 and 8 − 15 → 7 and −7) graded by value before the explanation opens, then a choice among three property names for each rewrite.
